335: On Saturday we went to the Military Forests Days in Ralsko, which was a trial by fire … or rather by water, for Vlasta, Michal Budský and Nikol Kabeláčová. Rain, a flat tyre on the trailer, more rain and luckily a roughly 20-minute window for the exhibition right at the end of the event. The guys at the Javornice festival had a longer drive, but Lukáš Valný, Ondra Nenadál and Tobík Dolák enjoyed the beautiful weather and the event and showed the locals how to jump over obstacles. Martin Šimůnek also spent his Saturday elsewhere near Ústí, going wild at a corporate event.
336: Photos for now are whatever we had, and hopefully something will arrive from the organisers, whom we thank for the invitation.
338: Season openers, exhibitions and workshops in Vísky u Letovic, Ostrava, Strážnice and Klánovice
339: September was all about pump track openings, racing and big exhibitions across the country. Martin Šimůnek and Michal Budský headed to a big Moravian-Silesian Region event at Trojhalí in Ostrava, where lots of concerts, workshops and performances took place in a beautiful setting.
340: The guys moved smoothly on to Strážnice, where the end of the cycling season was being celebrated, and again provided the local programme with two exhibition shows and a workshop, including hosting and the sound system.
341: Meanwhile Vlasta and Dalibor Šulc loaded the bikes and motorbikes and headed for Vísky u Letovic for the local village festival, where they put on exhibitions for a large audience from far and wide. They also battled the gravel, which complicated our show a little. Vlasta then went with the club kids to races in Thalheim, Germany, and the week before he did a marathon of coaching and more races in Slovakia.
342: At the beginning of October there was a big pump track opening in Prague-Klánovice. For Katarína Tóthová it was already one of several in a row, but this time, together with Vlasta and Marty, their task was to provide a complete 2-hour programme of exhibition, workshop and coaching – and they even threw in a mini race for the kids who came.
343: In October we also have the completion of the Říčany trail repairs, probably another Prague pump track opening and a club race in Tehov.
344: Exhibitions and workshops in Rasochy, Měšice and Lubné near Polička
345: At the end of the summer holidays and the start of the school year, besides coaching and training we also managed exhibitions. The first was at a cycling race in Rasochy, where a group of local bikers gathered for a traditional race around the area. Vlasta and Lukáš Valný coped with the uneven terrain and made full use of the space provided, to the organisers' satisfaction.
346: On the first Saturday of September Vlasta and Mára Tryner headed to nearby Měšice for the local festival, where we were the opening act for Kapitán DEMO and a few other bands and effectively closed an afternoon full of exhibitions and performances.
347: At the same time Martin Šimůnek and Matouš Balík went wild in Lubné near Polička, despite a small complication – they couldn't use their exhibition trailer. Luckily the obstacles are portable, so everything was sorted to the organiser's satisfaction. Both teams also had a bit of luck, because the weather wasn't ideal that day, but everything dried out nicely for the exhibitions. In the meantime Martin Šimůnek also managed several exhibitions and workshops 'around the house', as they say.
348: In the coming weeks we're in for a bit of a grind and some more big events. On top of that comes the repair of the trail we helped build in Říčany.
349: American car and motorbike meet at Pacov chateau
350: The beautiful chateau gardens in Pacov provided an unusual backdrop for a meet of American cars and motorbikes of all kinds. By the main stage there was an exhibition by kids from the club, Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček, Lukáš Valný and, on a motorbike, Dalibor Šulc. The scorching heat didn't stop us, and after the Pin-up girls were announced there was time to walk around the whole grounds. Thanks for the invitation.
352: Some projects just grab you right away. The Czech Database of Sports Coaches offered us a partnership and we gladly accepted.
353: The Czech Database of Sports Coaches offers an overview of coaches of individual and team sports, divided by regions of the Czech Republic. {1}Choose a coach according to your preferences{2} and get motivated to exercise and achieve your goals under expert guidance.
354: First outdoor exhibition and a Trial course
355: An outdoor exhibition in February? This year we kicked off the outdoor exhibition season really early, because a pig feast without bikes just isn't possible. Vlasta, Lukáš Valný and Matouš Balík headed for the beautiful little town of Janovice nad Úhlavou.
356: The weather was literally a lottery. Rain and freezing temperatures a few days before an exhibition make every Trial rider a bit nervous. Anyway, 12 degrees and partly cloudy in February with a great audience was our reward. A bit of wind was no problem and we rode a solid 30-minute show in front of an amazing crowd. As a reward there was a bit of the pig feast. Thanks for the invitation.
357: In 2023 too we put together a group of enthusiasts who wanted to try Trial and gain some experience for the coming season. January was marked by illness and other work, so we only started in February. What was special about the course this time wasn't so much the skill of the participants – who battled with their habits and the Trial bike like their lives depended on it – but the make-up of the riders. Friday was made up purely of men and Saturday, by contrast, purely of women and girls. Hopefully everyone gained something from it and lost nothing.
359: Martin Šimůnek is as busy as at the start of his career, so once again Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček was called up; he took Matouš Balík and his three offspring and set off for the children's day organised by the Municipal Police in Most. Lots of attractions and the pleasant setting of the children's traffic playground attracted relatively many visitors.
360: The boys and girls came on at the very end of the event. First they jumped for the local TV, then they started the exhibition, which included crashes and a bit of blood. Simply an adrenaline show. Fortunately it was only a scraped knee and some scratches on the shins. Thanks to Martin and the Municipal Police for the invitation.
361: Exhibition day in Kunratice, Škvorec and Jablonec nad Nisou
362: The weekend was 50/50 on whether weather apps work. Luckily they don't, so instead of the promised rain we rode all the booked events in two teams. Vlasta, Michal Budský, Ondřej Nenadál and later Lukáš Valný had the Kunratice Indian Summer and the Škvorec fair on their plate. Martin Šimůnek took Jablonec nad Nisou.
363: The Kunratice Indian Summer is a really successful mini-festival for kids and adults with concerts and loads of activities. The beautiful chateau park offered visitors just about everything you could think of at an event like this. In one longer show Vlasta, Michal and Ondra delivered a solid piece of action that entertained everyone present, including the organisers :). Vlasta tested a few setup changes on his new 26” trial bike. Michal Budský has ridden a street bike in recent years and Ondra represented the 20” trial bikes. So basically everything the Trial sport has to offer.
364: After the exhibition we moved quickly to Škvorec, where we were invited for the second time to the local festival called the Škvorec fair. Lukáš Valný joined us there and we took up a tactical spot in the middle of the grounds. The local green and park were packed and concerts were under way. Our job was to ride 2 shows. Space was a bit tight, but that wasn't a problem for us. In the second show there was even an interesting tug of war among the local women and girls over who would become the volunteer living obstacle. Honestly, that's probably never happened to us before :)
365: Martin sent a few photos from the event he rode in Jablonec nad Nisou, and evidently he had a decent crowd at this little corporate event too, as is usual for him.
369: Vlasta hopped up 199 steps of a lookout tower
370: A lookout tower record and two team exhibitions – Miskovice and Hořepník. Sometimes ideas come up that turn out to be very much on the edge.
371: {1}A lookout tower record and two team exhibitions – Miskovice and Hořepník{2}{3}{4}Sometimes ideas come up that turn out to be very much on the edge. One of them was the idea from Miskovice and Aleš Matoušek to try riding up the local 199-step lookout tower on a bike. The choice fell on Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček, holder of the record for riding up and down the Petřín lookout tower.
372: As it was an exhibition show, there was first a roughly 30-minute demonstration with egging on from Lukáš Valný and Tobík Dolák. Vlasta then took a few minutes' rest and set off to conquer the tower. Without any practice. The crisis came right after the first floor and only deepened. The steps were small for the larger diameter of mountain bike wheels, and the metal itself didn't help with grip either. In the end it took a third more hops than there were steps. From the second floor on: cramps and braking with two fingers. But the goal wasn't just to get to the top – which he did in 4:05 min – but also to get back down, and that's where the biggest problem arose. The Cube e-bike available was great, but the steps were small and had no barriers at the railings to prevent falls. Twice it already looked like a trip over the handlebars, arrow pointing down, because of the cramps in his hands, but luckily after two dabs Vlasta found his rhythm and rode down the floors partly on the front wheel, so he fitted safely. Down in 2:51 min, and an overall time of 6:56.74 min is beyond expectations given the preparation and conditions.{1} “After this I needed the whole day to pull myself together. I don't think I've ever been in worse physical shape after any sporting performance in my career, and physically it can't be compared with classic Trial. There, luckily, I do everything within 2 minutes and that's it. Thanks to the guys from the team, Aleš and my family for their help and support.”{2} said Vlasta, commenting on setting the record
373: On the same day Martin Šimůnek and Michal Budský rode an exhibition at a witch-burning night, making a pleasant trip to Hořepník. The weather was kind to them and the turnout was good, so thanks for the invitation and hopefully again next year.
374: Men Tune Up with Bikeskills no. 2
375: This year's last men's camp is behind us. Autumn is slowly taking its toll on attendance, and of course these dates aren't as popular. Moreover, we aimed this camp at more experienced riders. Besides the traditional morning in the park on the jumps, pump track and skills centre, we included a slightly sharper part on natural obstacles and trails.
376: The transfer was combined with a restaurant visit, and after a bit of a rest we set off for some proper rocks. The guys dropped like their lives depended on it (sometimes literally), but you could see progress towards more confidence. Hopefully everyone moved forward, gained more confidence and, we hope, motivation for the heap of things still to learn. For us the main thing in autumn was the experience and a bit of practice in patching tyres and cursing the sealant :)
378: Vlasta reports from the weekend marathon of events:
379: {1}I haven't had legs this sore after any weekend this year. On Saturday we were invited to the Around the Republic marathon race in Žacléř, where a group of cyclists set off on a course up to 1,500 km long (crazy people). After the start of the main category we jumped on the newly renovated square, including the new fountain (with permission from the mayor and the race director, of course).{2}
380: {1}The next exhibition was about 2 hours' drive away, but we said why not train in such beautiful sunny weather, which we haven't had much of this year. Our target was the nearest and relatively little-known Trial park of the Trutnov club, located at the Trutnov motocross club grounds. In the end we spent almost 2 hours there, including filming the most interesting little jumps.{2}{3}{4}https://www.instagram.com/tv/CS6gsLrlw9-/?utm_medium=copy_link{5}{6}{7}https://youtu.be/caAp7WWyPxs{8}
381: {1}Next we moved on to Rasochy, where about 125 bikers battled for trophies in XC races, including retro categories. The clods of turf in the meadow weren't a problem and the spectators created a great atmosphere, so we pulled out a few sharper tricks, like sitting on the handlebars, performed by Marek Tryner and Matouš Balík.{2}
382: {1}And on Sunday I had a lesson with a group of bikers that had already been rescheduled about 3 times, and which stretched from the original 4 hours to almost 8 hours including lunch. The guys went through the absolute basics, and we also threw ourselves at the pump track, forest obstacles and a few attempts on the jumps. To be continued next weekend.{2}
383: L'Etape, welcoming summer, Forestry Day and a children's day
384: We were riding on several fronts practically all weekend. On Saturday Martin Šimůnek and Míra Brunclík did the traditional Forestry Day near Česká Lípa. Michal Budský and Tobík Dolák, meanwhile, went wild on the folding obstacle set at a children's day in Český Jiřetín. And the biggest workload fell to Vlasta, Lukáš Valný and Nikolka Kabeláčová at one stop of the L'Etape amateur road races, followed by a transfer to the summer welcome in Doudleby nad Orlicí.
385: At first L'Etape was an intimate event, and our job was to entertain the spectators until the main part of the programme and the riders arrived. Of course we also entertained the organising team, whom we thank for the cooperation and hospitality. We had limited time, and after the exhibition only a few minutes to clear the area and flee ahead of the main peloton. Doudleby, by contrast, was a bigger event with a few hundred spectators, where we had a space next to the main stage and ran both an exhibition with volunteers – where the main star was the local history teacher – and a tape-jump contest, which ended in a draw between a local football star and Vlasta in a great atmosphere.
